note:
ISO 2026-W10 runs from March 2 through March 8. Saturn and Neptune are separated by about 0.8° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mercury and Venus are separated by about 3.0° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** 🌕 Full Moon · Sap Moon — 11:37:54 UTC. Bright moonlight favors prominent stars and planets while reducing contrast on faint deep-sky objects. Use Naos, Gamma-2 Vel as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -12.3; direct motion; 97.4% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Opposition in ecliptic longitude Mar 03 11:38 UTC. Mercury: In solar glare; magnitude 2.6; retrograde motion; 7.9% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Solar conjunction in ecliptic longitude Mar 07 11:01 UTC. Venus: In solar glare; magnitude -3.9; direct motion; 97.5% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Saturn in ecliptic longitude Mar 08 13:39 UTC. Conjunction with Neptune in ecliptic longitude Mar 07 11:27 UTC. Mars: In solar glare; magnitude 1.1; direct motion; 99.5% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 9.1; direct motion; 98.5% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -2.4; retrograde motion; 99.4% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 1.0; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Venus in ecliptic longitude Mar 08 13:39 UTC. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.7; direct motion; 99.9% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Neptune: In solar glare; magnitude 7.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Venus in ecliptic longitude Mar 07 11:27 UTC. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.6; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Binoculars:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified for binocular observing this week.

**Small telescope:** Concentrate on M48. Increase magnification only after the target and surrounding pattern are secure.

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

descriptors.name: Full Moon
descriptors.summary: Astronomical lunar phase near opposition to the Sun.
descriptors.body: Full Moon is the lunar phase in which the Moon and Sun are approximately opposite in geocentric ecliptic longitude, so the lunar disk is fully illuminated as seen from Earth.

story_candidates.dek: Naos is a stellar reference in Pup used by the weekly observing calendar.
story_candidates.body:
Why it is here: The Calendar selected Naos for this week’s fixed-sky observing sequence; its permanent object identity ties the weekly entry to the same star used by the finder.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Pup constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.
